stem.en: Two students each make an oxide of copper. Student X finds copper and oxygen in the mass ratio 4:1. Student Y finds them in the ratio 8:2. Do their results agree with the Law of Constant Proportions?

text.en: Yes. 8:2 is the same ratio as 4:1, so both students have the same compound.
No. The numbers are different, so they must have two different compounds.
We cannot say, because the law only holds for samples made in the same place.

explanation.en: Divide both numbers in 8:2 by 2 and you get 4:1, so Y simply used twice as much of each element. Option b compares the numbers and not the ratio. Option c is wrong because the law holds whatever the source of the compound.
